sources.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture-note chapter 1
sources.locator: Complete HTML Chapter 1 sections §1.2 through equation (1.5), §§1.3.1–1.3.4, and §§1.4.1–1.4.2; the exact section arguments and stated reservoir assumptions were read.

contents.name: §1.2: microcanonical preparation and entropy inequality (through equation 1.5)

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete microcanonical introduction through equation (1.5), including the equal-weight shell preparation and the entropy inequality argument.
source_review.supports: The conventional equal-weight microcanonical law and the fact that its preparation is a separate statistical assumption.
source_review.limitations: Tong uses a formal density-of-states notation in parts of the presentation; the local shell theorem defines a chart-based measure and proves its regular-level normalization. No time-average, ergodicity or empirical conclusion is taken from this source.

contents.name: §1.3.1: canonical distribution and partition function

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete derivation of the reservoir-weighted state law and normalization in §1.3.1.
source_review.supports: The canonical Boltzmann density and the partition function as its normalization.
source_review.limitations: The reservoir Taylor expansion is approximate. The local postulate adopts the normalized law only when its exact integral is finite and positive; no finite reservoir is claimed to produce it exactly.

contents.name: §1.3.2: canonical mean energy and energy fluctuations

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete partition-function derivative and variance calculation in §1.3.2.
source_review.supports: The canonical mean-energy derivative and the variance/heat-capacity identity.
source_review.limitations: Tong's differentiations are presented for the course's statistical models. The local theorem supplies uniform integrable envelopes for the continuous phase-space integrals.

contents.name: §1.3.3: Gibbs entropy of a canonical state

source_review.read_extent: Read the full entropy expression obtained by substituting the canonical probabilities into the Gibbs entropy.
source_review.supports: The canonical entropy formula in terms of log Z and mean energy.
source_review.limitations: The local result uses a dimensionless chosen reference measure and explicit integrability. The source's thermodynamic-limit ensemble-equivalence discussion is not consumed.

contents.name: §1.3.4: canonical free energy and its thermodynamic identities

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete free-energy definition and its derivative identities in §1.3.4.
source_review.supports: The finite canonical free-energy expression and its relationship to entropy and mean energy.
source_review.limitations: The local item does not differentiate with respect to the integer particle number and does not assert a macroscopic Euler relation.

contents.name: §1.4.1: grand-canonical distribution and sector-sum partition function

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete particle-exchange derivation and grand partition-function normalization in §1.4.1.
source_review.supports: The sector-weighted law proportional to exp[-β(H−μN)] and its partition function.
source_review.limitations: The local postulate requires convergence of the whole nonnegative sector sum and states no thermodynamic-limit equivalence.

contents.name: §1.4.2: grand potential and grand-canonical thermodynamic identities

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete grand-potential identity and its temperature and chemical-potential derivatives in §1.4.2.
source_review.supports: The finite grand potential and the entropy/particle-number derivative identities.
source_review.limitations: The local proof states the parameter held fixed in each derivative and supplies the uniform sector-sum moment bounds.

contents.name: §1.3.2: integration-by-parts equipartition argument

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete equipartition derivation and its integration-by-parts step.
source_review.supports: The identity relating a coordinate derivative of the Hamiltonian to the thermal scale.
source_review.limitations: The local lemma states absolute integrability and integrated boundary terms, including a finite-endpoint correction; the source idealizes vanishing tails.

contents.name: §1.2: density of states and the microcanonical shell

source_review.read_extent: Read the full microcanonical-shell discussion and its density-of-states convention.
source_review.supports: The regular-energy shell interpretation and energy disintegration motivation.
source_review.limitations: The local proof supplies a chart-based coarea measure and checks regularity, compactness, full-band flow hypotheses and the required AC premise.

contents.name: §1.3.4: derivatives of the partition function and fluctuations

source_review.read_extent: Read the parameter derivatives of the canonical partition function through the energy fluctuation identities.
source_review.supports: The mean and covariance interpretation of derivatives of a log-normalizer.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem proves the continuous-measure statement under explicit common integrable envelopes and does not assume formal differentiation.

contents.name: §1.3.2: Gibbs entropy and the variational inequality

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete entropy inequality argument and its equality condition.
source_review.supports: Nonnegativity of relative entropy and the canonical free-energy characterization.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem gives an extended-integral proof with explicit positivity, integrability and equality hypotheses.

sources.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture-note chapter 2
sources.locator: Complete HTML Chapter 2; §§2.2, 2.2.1, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4, with the classical ideal-gas phase-space integral, Gaussian momentum law, equipartition, finite counting convention and grand sum read in full.

contents.name: §2.2: classical ideal-gas phase-space partition function

source_review.read_extent: Read the classical ideal-gas partition integral and the position/momentum factorization in §2.2.
source_review.supports: The ideal-gas phase-space integral and Gaussian momentum factorization.
source_review.limitations: The local calculation retains the explicit action-scale reference and finite particle-counting convention rather than identifying a formal continuum cell count with an empirical quantity.

contents.name: §2.2.1: equipartition for unconstrained quadratic momentum coordinates

source_review.read_extent: Read the full Gaussian momentum integration and the resulting kinetic energy per quadratic degree of freedom.
source_review.supports: The conditional Gaussian momentum distribution and canonical quadratic momentum mean.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem gives explicit product-space hypotheses and boundary conditions and makes no claim for constrained coordinates or finite-shell preparations.

contents.name: §2.2.3: Gibbs paradox and species/counting conventions

source_review.read_extent: Read the full classical ideal-gas Gibbs-paradox discussion in §2.2.3.
source_review.supports: The dependence of the mixing-entropy account on species resolution and particle counting.
source_review.limitations: Tong's broad classical no-factorial comments are not treated as a universal theorem; the local example specifies the exact finite model and separates identical from distinguishable species.

contents.name: §2.2.4: ideal-gas grand-canonical sector sum

source_review.read_extent: Read the full ideal-gas grand-canonical partition and particle-number distribution calculation in §2.2.4.
source_review.supports: The exponential sector sum and Poisson particle-number law for the ideal-gas model.
source_review.limitations: The local example explicitly proves convergence of the series and states its finite-volume and finite-activity assumptions.

contents.name: §4.2.1: microcanonical distribution function

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §4.2.1 shell-law discussion, including the exact meaning of equal-weight energy-surface sampling and the source's time-average caveat.

source_review.limitations: Arovas uses formal delta-function notation in parts of the presentation; the local production theorem uses a chart-defined weighted shell measure and does not infer ergodicity.

source_review.read_extent: Read the full ideal-gas density-of-states derivation and the stated inverse-energy dimension in §4.2.2.

source_review.limitations: The local argument rederives the interacting kinetic-plus-potential marginal from radial pushforward and exact coarea; Arovas's formulas are not substituted for that proof.

contents.name: §4.4.1: ordinary canonical distribution and partition function

source_review.read_extent: Read the full canonical distribution and partition-function formulation in §4.4.1.
source_review.supports: The adopted fixed-N Boltzmann law and its normalization convention.
source_review.limitations: Arovas's quantum trace and thermodynamic-limit discussion are not imported; the local postulate is for a classical measurable phase space and finite normalization.

contents.name: §4.4.4: canonical averages

source_review.read_extent: Read the full canonical average-energy derivative in §4.4.4.
source_review.supports: The energy expectation as a derivative of the log partition function.
source_review.limitations: The local proof supplies the common integrable envelope required to differentiate a continuous phase-space integral.

contents.name: §4.4.5: canonical entropy and free energy

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete entropy/free-energy identity in §4.4.5.
source_review.supports: The canonical entropy and potential definitions under a fixed reference.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem retains the chosen dimensionless reference measure and finite-moment assumptions.

contents.name: §4.4.6: canonical fluctuations

source_review.read_extent: Read the full energy-variance and heat-capacity calculation in §4.4.6.
source_review.supports: The canonical variance response under fixed Hamiltonian controls.
source_review.limitations: The local statement is a finite-ensemble identity, not a thermodynamic-limit law or empirical heat-capacity claim.

contents.name: §4.5.1: grand-canonical distribution and partition function

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete grand-canonical distribution and sector sum in §4.5.1.
source_review.supports: The particle-exchange preparation law and the parameter βμ.
source_review.limitations: The local postulate states convergence of the entire sector integral rather than assuming it from sectorwise convergence.

contents.name: §4.5.2: grand-canonical entropy and potential

source_review.read_extent: Read the entropy/grand-potential identities in §4.5.2.
source_review.supports: The finite grand potential and its entropy and particle-number interpretation.
source_review.limitations: The local derivation uses explicit differentiability and integrability on the disjoint union of number sectors.

contents.name: §4.5.3: grand-canonical number and energy fluctuations

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete particle-number variance and energy-response formulas in §4.5.3.
source_review.supports: Grand-canonical covariance and number-fluctuation identities.
source_review.limitations: The local proof keeps distinct derivatives at fixed μ and fixed βμ and requires a common summable envelope over all sectors.

contents.name: §4.7.2: classical equipartition for a quadratic degree of freedom

source_review.read_extent: Read the full Gaussian integral and β derivative through equation (4.196), deriving one-half kBT per unrestricted quadratic coordinate.
source_review.supports: The canonical momentum component mean for a quadratic kinetic term.
source_review.limitations: The local proof states the unconstrained momentum domain and verified boundary/integrability conditions; it does not apply equipartition to constrained coordinates or exact finite shells.

contents.name: §4.2: phase-space measure and canonical shell conventions

source_review.read_extent: Read the phase-space volume convention and its relation to the classical shell law in the complete ensemble chapter.
source_review.supports: The Liouville phase-volume convention and the distinction between a labelled phase reference and physical particle counting.
source_review.limitations: The local item constructs cotangent geometry, sigma-finiteness and a measurable quotient explicitly; it does not import source shorthand as proof.

contents.name: §4.4: probability densities, expectations and statistical averages

source_review.read_extent: Read the ensemble definitions and the use of probability densities and expectation values in the complete chapter.
source_review.supports: The probability-law and density language used for classical ensembles.
source_review.limitations: The local definition includes general measure spaces, pushforwards and exact integrability requirements.

contents.name: §4.3: indistinguishability, particle counting and mixing entropy

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete finite-particle counting discussion and its Gibbs-paradox context.
source_review.supports: The conventional factorial counting factor and the role of operational species distinctions.
source_review.limitations: The item adopts a declared reference convention and does not treat the source discussion as a derivation of quantum indistinguishability.

contents.name: §4.2.2: ideal-gas shell density and momentum moments

source_review.read_extent: Read the exact quadratic ideal-gas density-of-states calculation and its energy dependence.
source_review.supports: The power-law shell density for a free quadratic gas.
source_review.limitations: The example retains finite action and counting references and compares two explicitly defined entropy conventions.

source_review.limitations: The local proof supplies a common integrable second-moment envelope, keeps the reference volume fixed, and makes no macroscopic equation-of-state claim.
